subject: Re: Pricing and next steps — SummitAI pilot unit economics
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@summitai.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: lina.gomez@summitai.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing follow-up from this morning's call

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Lina and I ran the session with our ML product team and we surfaced a couple of follow-up asks on cost:

- Can you sketch a plausible $/1M token target for a 3-month pilot (N = 50M tokens/month) vs a production band (N = 1B tokens/month)?
- We care about predictable monthly invoicing and an option to reserve capacity if we hit steady state. What are the discount levers for reserved vs on-demand?
- Can you send a simple invoice estimate we can show finance and procurement?

We are targeting an internal approval window by end of next week. If you can get a ballpark estimate and any assumptions (avg tokens per session, caching impact, expected latency SLOs) that would help.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, SummitAI

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@summitai.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up from this morning's call

Samir —

Great to connect today. Quick recap + the attached invoice sketch (SummitAI_estimate_v1.xlsx) — see summary below. I copied Ben (pricing lead) and Marissa (customer success) to help with the pilot SOW and procurement path.

High-level assumptions used in the estimate (spreadsheet tab "Assumptions"):
- Pilot length: 3 months; avg token volume: 50M tokens/month (burst to 80M)
- Prod bucket: modeled at 1B tokens/month as steady state
- Model family: rdx-large (open model equivalent of ~13B params) — latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms
- Caching: prefix/KV caching reduces billed tokens by ~12% for avg session mix (we show both raw and post-cache numbers)
- Batching & reserved capacity: assumed 10% efficiency gain in reserved pools vs on-demand

Pricing sketches (rounded):
- On-demand per-1M tokens: $95 — pilot band (50M/mo) => effective $/1M tokens shown in sheet (post-caching) = $86
- Reserved 6-mo commit (pilot to prod transition): quoted 18% discount => reserved effective = $70 / 1M tokens (1B band modeling uses additional volume tiers)
- Pilot fixed monthly invoice (example): base platform fee $2,500 + metered tokens at pilot rates (spreadsheet shows line items)

Key levers to reduce unit cost shown in the workbook:
1) Move from on‑demand to reserved pools (commit discounts + better batching)
2) Increase prefix caching coverage (we can share a short eval to measure cache-hit uplift)
3) Quantized model variants (we include a quantized rdx-large option in tab "Quantization")

Attachments and next steps:
- Attached: SummitAI_estimate_v1.xlsx (tabs: Assumptions, PilotInvoice, ProdBands, Sensitivity)
- Attached: Redwood_rate_card_Q2_2027.pdf (standard terms + reserved discounts)

Asks from your side:
- Can procurement/finance confirm whether you need net-30 billing vs PO-based invoicing?
- Who on your side will review the SOW (Marissa will draft a short pilot SOW once we confirm dates and billing cadence)?

If it helps I can turn the spreadsheet into a 1-page invoice mock we can send to finance. Available for a quick call tomorrow after 10am PT.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@summitai.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: lina.gomez@summitai.ai, procurement@summitai.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up from this morning's call

Thanks Olga — spreadsheet looks good at first pass. A few clarifying Qs from finance/procurement:

1) The sheet shows "post-cache" token counts. Can you also send the raw billed tokens vs metered tokens line? We need that split for our internal chargeback model.
2) For the reserved pricing, is the 18% discount a committed spend or committed compute-hours style (we prefer spend commitments tied to tokens).
3) If we do a 3-month pilot and then convert, does the pilot invoice apply toward the committed volume (i.e., credit execution)?

Also: Lina asked whether you can produce a single-page invoice mock that sums to a pilot monthly total with clear line items (platform fee, token line, expected credits). That helps speed approvals. Could you include an explicit "target $/1M tokens" cell in that mock for both pilot and prod bands?

If you can get those items to procurement by tomorrow EOD it would be ideal.

—Samir

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <samir@summitai.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, procurement@summitai.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up from this morning's call

Samir / Lina / procurement team —

Thanks for the questions. Quick answers and an attached 1-page invoice mock in the workbook (tab "PilotInvoice"):

1) Raw vs metered tokens: spreadsheet now includes both columns. Raw tokens = 100% of token activity; metered tokens = raw minus cache hits and internal batching credits. We show both monthly totals side-by-side and a derived effective $/1M tokens (pilot: $86 raw, $76 post-cache in the mock as an example).

2) Discount structure: the 18% is a spend-based commit (tokens-dollar equivalent over the commitment window). We can structure it as a token-dollar commit or a monthly minimum — procurement pick the preferred construct and we will mirror in the SOW.

3) Pilot credit toward commit: yes, pilot spend can be applied to the first 3 months of a longer commit if you choose to convert (we will include explicit credit language in the SOW).

Notes on the invoice mock:
- Pilot Monthly (example):
  - Platform fee (fixed): $2,500
  - Metered tokens (post-cache): 45M tokens @ $86 / 1M => $3,870
  - Estimate subtotal: $6,370
  - Taxes/fees: placeholder 8%
  - Estimated monthly total: $6,880 (rounded)

- Production band (1B tokens): example target $/1M tokens = $70 (reserved structure), annualized billing options are also available and shown in the "ProdBands" tab.

Next steps (I propose):
- I will: 1) export the sheet to a single PDF invoice-mock and 2) draft a short SOW for a 3-month pilot that includes the credit language.
- Marissa: will schedule a kickoff for the pilot technical onboarding and send the initial checklist.
- Procurement: if you can confirm billing cadence (net-30 or PO), I will route a DocuSign for signature — I attached a signing link in the related_links field for convenience.

If that plan sounds good I can get the PDF mock + SOW over by EOD.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
